channel.title: Praxia Blog: Notes from the Accounts
channel.description: Practical writing on PPC, tracking and lead quality from a freelance Google Ads, Microsoft Ads and GA4 specialist.

item.title: Your Conversion Count Is the Number Least Likely to Be Questioned
item.description: An account recorded 17,359 conversions in the time the business took roughly 4,500 bookings, and nobody ever asked, because high numbers go in the deck and low numbers get audited. How conversion counts drift from reality, what automated bidding does with a broken signal, and how to verify the pipeline with a real transaction.

item.title: What a GTM Consultant Actually Fixes
item.description: The problems a GTM consultant keeps fixing: enhanced conversions data stranded on the wrong page, AJAX forms that defeat submit triggers, Consent Mode loops, a CMP blocking the whole container, and when to move measurement server-side.

item.title: Smart Bidding Is Only as Smart as What You Feed It
item.description: Target CPA and target ROAS treat every recorded conversion as the truth. When the Conversions column contains spam leads, duplicate fires and soft actions promoted to primary, bidding does not just misreport: it steers budget toward the junk. How each pollution distorts delivery, and the order to fix it in.

item.title: What Actually Breaks When You Restructure Google Ads Accounts via the API
item.description: Real restructures are thousands of operations that depend on each other, and the work lives in what the tutorials skip: partial failure handling that turns errors into a fixable list, MutateOperation batching, and the ordering rules around temporary resource IDs.

item.title: Why I Stopped Using the Keyword Planner UI and Built My Own Tooling
item.description: The Keyword Planner UI works for occasional research and breaks down across many accounts and markets. How querying the API directly turns keyword research into one repeatable run whose output feeds restructures, negative lists and asset briefs.

item.title: AI-Generated Fake Leads: Why They Look Completely Real and How to Stop Them
item.description: A new breed of form spam is hitting lead-gen advertisers: enquiries with real company names, coherent messages and valid contact details, carrying a phishing link as the payload. Why filters miss them and the fixes that remove most of it for very little effort.
